title: Figma Masters Class
description: A full Figma apprenticeship: frames, layout systems, components, variants, prototyping, and handoff-ready UI craft from blank canvas to developer-ready specs.

lessons.title: Figma Mindset: Structure Before Decoration

introduction.text: Great Figma files are systems, not artboards of one-offs. Start with frames, spacing rhythm, and hierarchy before shadows and flourishes. Name layers. Think in reusable parts. This apprenticeship trains end-to-end product UI craft—from wire to polished, handoff-ready screens.

questions.question: Named layers help:
options: You and teammates navigate the file
questions.correctAnswer: You and teammates navigate the file

project.title: File Hygiene Starter
project.description: Create a starter file structure: Cover page, Foundations (type/color/spacing), Components, Screens, and Archive. Document naming rules for frames and layers in a sticky note on the cover.

questions.question: Spacing rhythm means:
options: Consistent spacing scale across the UI
questions.correctAnswer: Consistent spacing scale across the UI

questions.question: Reusable parts mindset prepares you for:
Archive pages exist to:
options: Park old explorations without cluttering active screens
questions.correctAnswer: Park old explorations without cluttering active screens

objectives: Explain the main idea of "Figma Mindset: Structure Before Decoration" without looking at notes
Identify one mistake beginners make on this topic and how to avoid it
Complete a concrete artifact for: File Hygiene Starter
keyTakeaways: Great Figma files are systems, not artboards of one-offs.
Check understanding with practice before you build.

lessons.title: Frames, Grids, and Auto Layout

introduction.text: Auto Layout is how modern Figma UI survives content changes. Learn direction, gap, padding, and hugging vs filling. Combine with layout grids for page rhythm. Resize like a product, not a poster: components must flex without manual nudging.

options: Direction, gap, padding, and resizing behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Direction, gap, padding, and resizing behavior

questions.question: Fill container is useful when:
options: Items should expand into available space
questions.correctAnswer: Items should expand into available space

questions.question: Manual nudging everywhere is a sign:

questions.question: Gap vs padding:

questions.correctAnswer: Gap spaces children; padding spaces inside the parent edge

lessons.title: Typography, Color, and Foundations

introduction.text: Foundations are the tokens of your file: type styles, color styles, and spacing habits. Limit the palette. Define text styles for roles (display, title, body, caption). Accessibility starts here—contrast and readable sizes are not optional polish.

questions.question: Contrast matters because:
options: People need to read the UI
questions.correctAnswer: People need to read the UI

lessons.title: Components, Variants, and Instances

introduction.text: Components encode reusable UI. Variants express states (default/hover/disabled) and types (primary/secondary) without duplicating frames. Prefer properties over sprawling variant matrices when possible. Instances should be nudged via properties, not detached chaos.

questions.question: Variants commonly represent:
options: States and types of one component
questions.correctAnswer: States and types of one component

questions.question: Detaching instances casually causes:
options: Lost updates when the main changes
questions.correctAnswer: Lost updates when the main changes

questions.question: A button set should include:
options: Key states like default and disabled
questions.correctAnswer: Key states like default and disabled

project.title: Button + Input Library
project.description: Build a small library: Button (primary/secondary × default/disabled) and Input (default/focus/error). Use Auto Layout. Document instance rules on the library page (when not to detach).

questions.question: Main component updates should:
options: Flow to instances that were not detached
questions.correctAnswer: Flow to instances that were not detached

questions.question: Error input state should show:
options: Clear error affordance and helper text pattern
questions.correctAnswer: Clear error affordance and helper text pattern

questions.question: Icons in buttons are best handled via:
Masters component craft means:
options: Consistent UI that scales across screens
questions.correctAnswer: Consistent UI that scales across screens

lessons.title: Flows, Prototypes, and Critique

introduction.text: Screens without flows hide UX problems. Prototype key paths: happy path and one failure path. Use critique prompts focused on clarity, hierarchy, and next action—not taste wars. Record decisions so the file remains a product artifact.

questions.question: A flow is:
options: A connected user journey across screens
questions.correctAnswer: A connected user journey across screens

questions.question: Severity-ranked issues help teams:
options: Fix the highest impact problems first
questions.correctAnswer: Fix the highest impact problems first

lessons.title: Handoff: Specs, Assets, and Dev Collaboration

introduction.text: Handoff is a conversation with evidence: spacing, type, states, and assets. Use inspect-friendly structure, export rules, and a short handoff note covering behavior not visible in static frames. Reduce “design intent” guesswork—masters deliver clarity developers can build.

questions.question: Behavior notes cover:
options: Interactions and edge cases not obvious in stills
questions.correctAnswer: Interactions and edge cases not obvious in stills

project.title: Handoff Packet
project.description: Prepare a handoff packet for a settings screen: annotated spacing, component list, exportable icons, and a one-page behavior note (toggles, validation, empty). Write three questions you would ask engineering in kickoff.

options: Design and eng share the same asset language
questions.correctAnswer: Design and eng share the same asset language
